beats.t: In an instant, the water rose to their knees, then their waists. Holding their breath, books floated up and drifted away.
OIIINK! My feet! I can't touch the bottom!
Pigs float! Stay calm. You're a swim ring right now!
Yeoni flailed. Their body floated, but it would not move as they wished. The current kept pulling them between the shelves.
The middle of the water suddenly went still. A black spine slowly surfaced there.
The black tiger. Droplets clung to the tips of its fur, and the golden ring at its neck shone wetly.
It would have been better if it had ended upstairs. But you had to follow me down.
Give my book back! My name was on the borrowing card!
Cards blur when they get wet. Names, too.
The tiger struck the surface with a paw. Water rose like a wall and swallowed an entire bookshelf.
(Hold on. Wood has roots. I just need to put down roots.)
Green roots stretched from Yeoni's hooves, searching for the floor. But they lost their way in the water and floated upward.
They won't hold. My roots can't find the bottom!
There's too much water! When water overflows, it carries Wood away, roots and all. Excess Water Sets Wood Adrift—水多木漂!
Give me a life jacket, not a proverb!
The next wave swallowed Yeoni. Their small body was sucked between the shelves.
Yeoni.
Yeongnyangi plunged in without hesitation. But the moment his fluffy fur soaked up water, his small body began sinking like a stone.
Mr. Cat! Metal generates Water, so water drains your strength! Metal generates Water—金生水!
I know. I know, but does that matter right now?
Yeongnyangi gritted his teeth and paddled. For every handspan forward, he sank two.
Oh, honestly. Everyone move. Who here can actually swim?
Moka clamped his ladle between his teeth and slipped underwater. One sweep of his violet tail like an oar split the current.
You're coming at an otter with water? This is my front yard.
Moka grabbed a fistful of the sinking Yeongnyangi's cloak collar and pulled him up. Dangling from the otter's hand, the drenched cat broke the surface.
Let go of the cloak. Being dragged by the scruff is beneath a cat's dignity.
Find your dignity after the water drains. For now, just breathe, you heavy lump of iron.
Find Yeoni first. Not me.
I know, I know. But I've got to fish you out before I fish out the pig. If you both sink, that's two round trips for me.
Moka pushed Yeongnyangi onto a floating bookshelf, then threw himself back into the water. This time downward, toward where Yeoni had vanished.
Underwater, all was quiet. Soaked books drifted slowly like jellyfish, and someone's memories glimmered faintly between their pages.
(Breathe. Support the breath. Yeongnyangi said so. Don't pull it up. Set it down on the ground.)
Yeoni stopped flailing their hooves. As they relaxed, the current stopped shoving them and wrapped around them instead.
Right ahead, an old umbrella drifted upside down. It was exactly like the one Yeoni had left abandoned in the corner of their attic room.
A torn page clung beneath it. A bus stop in the rain. Two people under one umbrella. Their faces were blurred by water.
(Is that... me? It looks like me, but I don't remember this.)
A black paw snatched the page. The tiger stared at Yeoni from directly ahead. Even underwater, its voice rang clear.
Don't look. That isn't for you to see.
Why? It's a book borrowed in my name. Why do you get to decide?
Some debts are better left unknown. Especially ones you can never repay.
(This smell. The rain smell from the card. You were the one who erased the borrower's name.)
Do you know me? You've acted like you know me ever since we first met.
No. And I don't need to. I only collect what's written in the ledger.
Liar. If it was just something in your ledger, why did you hide that page so quickly?
The tiger's red eyes wavered for a moment. They alone seemed untouched by the water.
The tiger crumpled the page in its paw. Yet the movement was strangely careful. As though hiding it, not throwing it away.
Then the darkness at the bottom split. Five black fingers rose like seaweed and wrapped around the tiger's ring.
What are you hesitating for? Sink that pig.
You said I only needed to retrieve the book. As for the pig...
That is an order. The price for leaving an uncollected entry in your ledger.
The golden ring tightened. The tiger caught a short breath, then raised its paw and laid it on Yeoni's head.
(It's pressing me. Down, down.)
But the paw did not press immediately. For one beat, one very short beat, the tiger stayed still.
Get that paw off, Stripes!
Moka charged through the current. He lashed the tiger's side with his tail, then seized Yeoni's scruff in his teeth and pulled them up.
The baby dragon on Yeoni's wrist snapped its eyes open. It looked at the water once, then opened its mouth wide.
The dragon began drinking. A whirlpool streamed into its tiny mouth, and the water swallowing the shelves swiftly receded.
The drained library floor was sodden as mud. Soaked books lay scattered everywhere, catching their breath in thin gasps.
This little thing drank all that water?
Chen Earth is a storehouse for water. 辰 is the earth that holds water in. That dragon didn't come to you by chance, my lady.
Its belly's going to burst. Hey, dragon. How many liters did you drink?
With its belly bulging, the baby dragon curled around Yeoni's wrist again. Then it gave a small burp of water droplets.
Five stars. No, six. Even if it breaks the rating rules.
At the far end of the muddy floor, the tiger stood on the landing leading down. The ring at its neck still glowed red-hot.
I didn't know you traveled with a dragon, too. That won't work next time, either.
Why did you stop earlier? When it told you to push me down. You stopped for one beat.
You imagined it. Everything looks slow underwater.
The tiger turned away. Before descending, it drew its clenched paw once toward its chest, like someone protecting something from getting wet.
Its black tail vanished into the darkness below. Only wet pawprints continued down, one step at a time.
At the water's edge, Yeongnyangi shook himself. With his fur plastered to his body, he looked half his usual size. Water dripped from his hat's tassel. Coughing, he stood.
Mr. Cat! Are you okay? Did you swallow much water?
I'm fine. Moka saved my life. Don't make me say it twice.
Should've recorded that. I could've milked it for the rest of my life.
Yeoni looked at Yeongnyangi's left paw. A stain like red rust spread over the scorched patches. He quickly hid it beneath his cloak.
That paw. It's been strange for a while. Show me.
It's because it's wet. Iron rusts when it gets wet, too. It'll be better once it dries.
Yundal glanced at Yeongnyangi. He said nothing. Instead, he pushed his gloved hand deep into his pocket.
(They all know something. There's something only I don't know.)
The soaked books struggled to breathe on the floor. Some had pages stuck together, blocking their airways.
Leave them like this, and they'll all stiffen up. But we saw what happened with fire earlier.
That's because you used too much heat. Pig, do you bake bread with the heat turned all the way up?
No. Then the outside burns and the inside stays raw.
Exactly. Drying books is the same. Low and slow. About as warm as your palm.
Yeoni gently rested a hoof on a book. Instead of flames, they slowly let warmth flow through. Warm as a quilt laid in the sunshine.
The stuck pages separated one by one. The wet book gave a little cough, then began breathing again.
It worked! It's breathing. Moka, are you actually a genius?
Only noticing now? Cooking is the study of handling fire. Rap is the study of handling breath.
Expression helping Resources. Using fire to dry soaked memories—this may be a first in the library's history.
Yeoni looked down at what they held. A corner of the page the tiger had crumpled and taken had caught on their hoof and stayed behind.
A scrap the size of a fingernail. The edge of an upturned umbrella. And one tiny line of writing. Let's share the umbrella.
(Let's share. Who said that to whom?)
A staircase emerged beneath the wall as the water drained. Wet golden writing hung above its entrance.
[ Basement Level 3 · Things That Have Not Happened · Read with Caution ]
The shelves of things that haven't happened. Even I've never gone down here. They say those are memories no one has lived yet.
The tiger went down, too. There are wet pawprints on the stairs.
Yeoni folded the scrap and tucked it inside their hoof. A faint sound like rain came from below.
Let's go down. My spring is down there.
Let's go. But if there's water this time, I'm rescuing the pig before the cat. Changing the order.
The baby dragon on Yeoni's wrist hugged its swollen belly and gave a little cry. Somewhere below, someone folded an umbrella.
